headline: US stocks ended mixed in holiday-shortened session as soft payrolls data eased Fed hike fears and rotation from tech into value and cyclicals continued
raw_text:
- Dow Jones Industrial Average rose more than 500 points to a record close near 52,900 while the S&P 500 was flat and the Nasdaq Composite declined
- June nonfarm payrolls increased by about 57,000 jobs, well below forecasts near 110,000, with a downward revision to May reinforcing a cooling labor market
- Softer jobs data lowered near-term Fed rate-hike odds and supported expectations for a steady policy stance focused on inflation rather than labor weakness
- Information technology was the worst-performing sector as investors rotated out of technology and chip names into value and cyclical groups
- Semiconductor stocks fell, with names including SanDisk (SNDK), Applied Materials (AMAT), Micron (MU), Marvell (MRVL), and AMD (AMD) extending losses amid pressure on AI-related plays
- Tesla (TSLA) declined despite beating Q2 delivery expectations, adding to weakness across high-growth, tech-oriented stocks
- Healthcare, consumer staples, utilities, energy, financials, and communication services sectors led gains, with seven of 11 S&P sectors closing higher
- Small-cap and value-oriented stocks outperformed, aided by sector rotation that also lifted software names including Apple (AAPL), Adobe (ADBE), Workday (WDAY), and Fair Isaac (FICO)
- No major after-hours earnings moves above roughly 2% were reported, and focus shifts to limited US data on July 7, follow-through from the jobs report, and upcoming inflation readings and Fed commentary
